headline: 100,000+ WordPress sites hacked in supply chain attack, FIM tools reported 100% clean
summary: A coordinated attack compromised over 100,000 WordPress sites by exploiting third-party cloud infrastructure, bypassing traditional File Integrity Monitoring.
details: Over 100,000 WordPress sites were simultaneously compromised in a single, coordinated supply chain attack. This occurred despite File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) tools reporting zero modifications and a 100% clean status.
The attackers did not tamper with the official WordPress.org plugin repository. Instead, they targeted the vendor's upstream cloud infrastructure, specifically a DigitalOcean Spaces bucket.

This bucket powered dynamic promotional banners within the BigOpti component, shipped with BdThemes plugins. By gaining write access, attackers served poisoned JSON responses directly to end-user servers.
The BigOpti component fetched JSON data containing a display_id parameter. The application failed to sanitize or escape this parameter on the client side before rendering it in wp-admin.

Because the input was rendered live as executable code, an XSS payload triggered silently the moment any logged-in administrator opened their WordPress dashboard. Zero clicks were required from the attacker.

The exploit initiated automated routines, including extracting the target site's hostname and using a Base36 hashing algorithm to derive deterministic admin credentials on demand. Knowing only the URL allowed instant calculation of valid admin logins.

Standard FIM tools scan local disk files against pristine source code checksums. Since the core plugin files on disk matched official versions, local scanners saw no anomalies; the malicious payload was pulled dynamically at runtime over the network.

headline_marked: [[Claude Cowork is now available]] in the Chrome sidebar extension
headline: Claude Cowork is now available in the Chrome sidebar extension
summary: The change integrates conversations into user history and enables skills/connectors directly in the browser. Max and Team subscribers get access today, with Pro plans following soon.
details: Anthropic's Claude Cowork is now fully integrated into the company's Claude for Chrome browser extension. This significant update means that any conversations held within the Chrome side panel will become part of the user's history.

Furthermore, all user-defined skills and connectors will automatically function within the browser environment. This integration also allows users to seamlessly start tasks in a dedicated Claude app and continue them in a Chrome browser, or vice versa.

The new feature is immediately accessible to Max and Team subscribers, with access for Pro plan users rolling out in the coming weeks. This provides a helpful upgrade for anyone who frequently performs tasks within the Google-owned browser.

This integration offers a way for the chatbot to execute tasks in various tools, even those that do not have direct official support from Anthropic. Claude Cowork was designed as a more streamlined option for general users, complementing the professional-grade Claude Code.
Anthropic recently enhanced Claude Cowork with the capability for smartphone control. The broader Claude for Chrome extension was initially rolled out to all Anthropic users in late 2025.
